---
title: "SAF Architecture Framework"
---

This is the full Statistical Architecture Framework document, split into chapters. It is the reference: everything the workgroup has agreed about how a statistical office can describe its production architecture. You do not need to read it in order, and most readers never read all of it.

If you are new to SAF, start with [SAF in Brief](../SAF-in-Brief.qmd) instead, then come back here for the chapter you need. Terms are explained in the [Glossary](../glossary.qmd).

::: {.callout-note title="About this document"}
{{< include _document-info.md >}}

A few sections are still marked as not yet written. That is deliberate — the framework is a living document.
:::

## The chapters

**The foundations** — why SAF exists and what it is built on.

| Chapter | What it covers | Who needs it |
|---|---|---|
| [Introduction and Scope](introduction.qmd) | What SAF is for, what it covers and what it deliberately does not prescribe, and who it is written for | Everyone, first |
| [Motivation](motivation.qmd) | The pressures driving change, the goals, the eleven architecture principles, the outcomes and the stakeholders | Managers, policy makers, privacy officers |
| [Strategy](strategy.qmd) | The capability model (what an office must be able to do) and the ten value streams | Architects, planners |

**The business architecture** — how the production chain actually works. This is the part most readers come for.

| Chapter | What it covers | Who needs it |
|---|---|---|
| [Business Architecture](business-architecture.qmd) | The reference actors and roles, business processes and functions, and the reference models for the value chain | Architects, process owners |
| [Steady-State Architecture](steady-state.qmd) | The five steady states of data, their quality gates, metadata and the rules common to all states | Everyone working with production |
| [Statistical Data Value Chain](value-chain.qmd) | How the chain works: the four process types, the standard activities, and how the principles apply across the chain | Everyone working with production |

**The ten value streams in depth** — one chapter each. Each follows the same ten attributes: purpose, position and state transition, stages, the four process types, actors and roles, capabilities and processes, principles, interfaces and events, key performance indicators, and examples. Maturity checklists and end-to-end scenarios are in the [Toolkit](../toolkit.qmd#value-stream-instruments).

*The six production streams, in the order data passes through them:*

| Chapter | Takes data from → to |
|---|---|
| [VS-01 Data Acquisition and Ingestion](vs-01.qmd) | Source data → #1 Raw |
| [VS-02 Data Standardization and Integration](vs-02.qmd) | #1 Raw → #2 Standardized |
| [VS-03 Data Editing and Enrichment](vs-03.qmd) | #2 Standardized → #3 Processed |
| [VS-04 Estimation, Analysis, and Statistical Modeling](vs-04.qmd) | #3 Processed → #4 Statistics |
| [VS-05 Statistical Product Composition](vs-05.qmd) | Within #4, to an approved product |
| [VS-06 Dissemination and Service Delivery](vs-06.qmd) | #4 → #5 Released → #6 Consumed |

*The four supporting streams, which run continuously across the whole chain:*

| Chapter | What it provides |
|---|---|
| [VS-07 Governance and Compliance](vs-07.qmd) | Frameworks, controls and assurance |
| [VS-08 Innovation and Methodological Development](vs-08.qmd) | Validated new methods and tools |
| [VS-09 Infrastructure and Platform Enablement](vs-09.qmd) | Platforms, environments, integration |
| [VS-10 Customer and Stakeholder Engagement](vs-10.qmd) | Understood user needs and relationships |
